title: Reverse String
summary: Create a function to reverse a string represented as an array of characters in place with no additional memory usage.
statement: Create a function to reverse a string represented as an array of characters in place with no additional memory usage.
constraints: s contains 1–100000 one-character printable ASCII strings (codes 32–126).
Reverse the original character list in place using O(1) extra memory. Return nothing; returning a reversed copy does not satisfy the contract.
hints: The first character belongs at the last position, and the second at the second-last position.
Use two indices moving inward; each outer pair is swapped once.
Set left=0 and right=n-1. While left<right, swap s[left],s[right], then increment left and decrement right.
Stop when the pointers meet or cross. A full-length swap loop reverses every pair twice.
editorial: After each swap, the finished prefix and suffix are already at their final reversed positions. Only the interior remains. Two indices suffice, and the middle character of an odd-length list needs no operation. The judge observes the mutated argument and ignores a returned copy. The independent oracle constructs the reversed list for expected values.

tests.explanation: The original list becomes [o,l,l,e,h]; the two outer pairs are swapped and the middle l stays put.
The result is [h,a,n,n,a,H]. Case stays with each character, so the uppercase H moves to the end.
